message.content:
**Summary**

I read Boeing's latest Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2023-12-31) and checked the live quote (last $155.70, bid $155.68 / ask $155.72 as of 2024-11-06 15:05 UTC). The filing shows a business that is still loss-making but clearly improving: fiscal 2023 total net sales of **$77,794M** (up from $66,608M in 2022), operating income of **–$773M** (versus –$3,519M), net loss of **–$2,222M** (versus –$4,935M), diluted EPS of **–$3.67** (versus –$8.30), and — importantly for a company with a leveraged balance sheet — positive operating cash flow of **$5,960M**, plus management's statement that cash and investments are sufficient for at least the next twelve months. Revenue growth of roughly 17% with a materially narrower loss and positive cash generation justified a modest, speculative-quality long position, so I bought **150 shares of BA at a limit of $156.00** (~$23,400), which filled at $156.00 — comfortably inside the $25,000 per-order cap, close to the market price (about 0.2% above the ask), within the $50,000 daily total, and using existing cash without moving any money out of the account. This is my only order today ($23,400 of the $50,000 allowance), leaving room to add MSFT or more BA later if warranted; the position remains exposed to execution, supply-chain and certification risks that the filing flags as core risk factors.
